headline_marked: Video shows [[robbers cut rickshaw passenger's pocket]] with knife in Chattogram
headline: Video shows robbers cut rickshaw passenger's pocket with knife in Chattogram
summary: Two muggers stole money and a mobile phone from a passenger, using a knife to cut the victim's pocket when they couldn't retrieve an item.
details: A shocking video has surfaced on social media showing two muggers robbing a rickshaw passenger in Chattogram. The incident took place at Satish Babu Lane, behind the Kotwali Police Station.

The footage shows the attackers using a knife to cut the passenger's right pocket after failing to retrieve an item by hand. During the struggle, one of the muggers is seen stabbing the victim's left leg with the knife.
The passenger is heard saying, 'Brother, I am giving it,' as the robbers forcibly took his money and mobile phone.
The crime was interrupted when residents from nearby buildings began shouting 'Hit them, hit them!' causing the robbers to flee the scene in a battery-powered auto-rickshaw.
Kotwali Police Station OC Abu Zayed Mohammad Nazmun Nur told Prothom Alo that while the police have seen the video, no victim has come forward to file a complaint.
The police have since increased patrols in the area to prevent further incidents.

headline_marked: Trump [[bans CNN, MS NOW and Politico]] from White House over 'fake news'
headline: Trump bans CNN, MS NOW and Politico from White House over 'fake news'
summary: The US President accused the outlets of spreading fiction and lies, while critics call the move an illegal assault on press freedom.
details: US President Donald Trump announced a ban on CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from the White House, accusing the outlets of spreading 'fake news' about his administration.
Trump stated on Truth Social that the ban is effective immediately, arguing that media outlets should not be able to report 'fiction and lies' when covering the US President.
In the Oval Office, Trump explained the move was based on 'cumulative stories' over the last two years, claiming the outlets purposely write negative news to diminish the Republican administration.
US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth backed the ban, accusing the news organizations of having 'endangered troops' through their reporting.
The affected news outlets have condemned the move, with CNN calling it an 'illegal assault' on press freedom and Politico vowing to defend its First Amendment rights.
The White House Correspondents Association stated it stands in defense of the journalists being singled out for doing their jobs.
Legal experts, including Bruce Brown of the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, have called the ban 'flatly unconstitutional' and 'textbook viewpoint discrimination.'
This move comes as Trump faces record low approval ratings and potential losses for the Republican Party in the upcoming November midterm elections.
